Subject: MSA redline — clarification needed on output use & marketing

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal is reviewing the MSA and the order form and they flagged a couple of items we need to clarify before procurement can sign:

1) Output ownership / product use — the current redwood draft says outputs are "subject to Customer rights" but also includes a broad "product improvement" clause. We need explicit confirmation that Acropolis retains exclusive rights to clinical content generated from our data and that Redwood will not use those outputs for model training without our opt-in.

2) Marketing/attribution — our privacy/comms team is OK with logo + short customer reference, but legal wants a carveout so any public case study requires an additional approval step and content sign-off.

3) Feedback license — please confirm whether the feedback license applies to anonymized telemetry only or includes content excerpts.

I've attached our markup (MSA_redlines_v2) and a suggested clause from counsel. Can we get a short call with your legal to land on language? We are hoping to close this week.

Best,
Sara Lane
Head of Partnerships
Acropolis Health

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear notes and for sending counsel's suggested language. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Product) so we can give a consolidated answer.

Quick reply to set expectations:
- Output ownership: our standard position is the customer retains rights to their customer content (including outputs derived solely from that content). We also have a separate feedback/telemetry license that covers aggregate/telemetry signals used to improve models.
- Training opt-in: we can commit to an opt-in for training on customer-specific data (i.e., explicit agreement required).
- Marketing: we respect approvals for customer stories — we can add a clause requiring written approval for any public case study or logo usage.

Laura/Karthik — can one of you propose redline language that preserves the above while keeping the platform improvements clause workable (so we can still improve general model quality without using Acropolis's protected outputs)? Sara, would a short ~30 minute call tomorrow afternoon work to finalize?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: MSA redline — proposed language for output/training/marketing

Sean / team — drafting notes below and attached a short plain-language clause you can drop into the MSA/order form. Key principles I used:

- Customer Content & Outputs: Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and of Outputs that consist solely of or are derived specifically from Customer Content; Redwood will not claim title to such Outputs.
- Training & Feedback: Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs for model training or to improve models unless Customer opts in via an explicit checkbox in the Order Form or a mutually-signed addendum. We will, however, retain the right to use anonymized telemetry (performance metrics, anonymized system logs) to improve service reliability.
- Marketing/Attribution: Redwood may not use Customer name, logo, or a case study without prior written consent; short references in a customer list are permitted unless Customer objects in writing.

Suggested redline text (plain):
"Customer Content and Outputs: Except as set forth in this Section, Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and to any Outputs that are the result of processing Customer Content. Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Outputs for model training or to improve any model without an express, written opt-in from Customer.

Telemetry: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and use anonymized and aggregated telemetry data and service metrics for the sole purpose of improving the performance and reliability of Redwood's services, provided such data does not contain Customer Content or verbatim Outputs."

I'll attach this as Acropolis_requested_clause.txt and the Word redline is updated with the same language. Karthik — product is OK with the opt-in approach; we should add an operational note about how opt-in will be reflected in the order form UI and the SLA/retention options.

Laura Bennett

Subject: Final proposal: opt-in training clause + marketing approvals (ACR-2028-042)

Sara / Jon — thanks for the patience. Per Laura's text (attached) we propose the following for the MSA + Order Form for Acropolis Health (high level):

1) Outputs & ownership
- Confirmed: Acropolis retains ownership of Customer Content and any Outputs derived from that content. Redwood will not claim title to those Outputs.

2) Training / feedback license
- Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs for model training or improvements unless Acropolis opts in explicitly. Opt-in will be captured either by (a) a checkbox in the Order Form that references the training addendum or (b) an executed Data Use Addendum.
- Redwood may use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for platform reliability; we will commit to a telemetry sampling/retention notice in the Order Form.

3) Marketing & attribution
- Redwood will not use Acropolis name, logo, or publish a case study without prior written consent. We will maintain a short customer list for sales collateral; Acropolis can opt out of the list in writing.

Next steps:
- I attached the updated redline (MSA_redlines_v3.docx) and the plain text clause (Acropolis_requested_clause.txt).
- If the language looks good to you, can legal send a quick confirmation email and we will push the Order Form with the opt-in checkbox to DocuSign (link below). If you prefer one call to sign off, happy to schedule 30 minutes Monday.
